records.name: Math Contest at Penn
records.summary: Penn students who run a math contest for high schoolers, with problems meant for beginners and experienced students alike. The site does not list volunteer roles, so ask the staff by email.
records.what_you_do: Have a high schooler compete in the contest, in person on Penn's campus or online, or join the interest list to hear about the next one. Ask staff by email about helping on the contest team.

schedule.text: The site posts no dates for its contests. Join the interest list or email staff to hear when the next one is set.

cost.text: The site does not state an entry fee.

first_step.how: Join the PMC VI interest list from the homepage, or email staff@pennmathcontest.com with questions.
first_step.basis: The interest list and the staff email are open to anyone, and the site says the problems suit beginners. The site describes no orientation or volunteer steps.
first_step.what_to_expect: Contests have individual and team challenges, with problems meant for every level. Students take part in person on Penn's campus or online, and winners get prizes or certificates. The site does not give contest dates, length, or fees, so the staff email is the best way to ask.
first_visit_tips: Join the interest list so you hear when the next contest is announced.
Email staff to ask whether a high schooler can take part in person or online.

records.notes: No dated evidence of a 2026 contest on the site. The past results and archive pages name PMC V with no date or year, and PMC VI has only an interest list. Volunteer roles are not described anywhere on the site, so the tier 1 wording was softened to ask staff. The summary and schedule were corrected to match the site. The interest list is an online form that was not opened or submitted.

records.name: Mayfair Holmesburg Parade Committee
records.summary: The volunteer committee that puts on the Mayfair and Holmesburg Thanksgiving Parade each November. Neighbors can carry a banner, march, or enter a homemade float.
records.what_you_do: Carry a banner (7th grade and older; banner carriers earn 6 community service hours), apply to march in the parade, or build a homemade float and enter it for a best-float ribbon.

schedule.text: The parade is held on a Sunday in late November, from 12 to 3 pm.

cost.text: The parade page names no fee.

first_step.how: Email info@thanksgivingparade.org to sign up as a banner carrier, or fill in the parade application form (a PDF on the site) and email it to the same address.
first_step.basis: Anyone can apply by email to march, carry a banner, or enter a float. The site names no beginner program, orientation, or practice.
first_step.what_to_expect: Marchers and banner carriers gather at staging areas along the route before the noon start. The site's order of march page says units can begin assembling around 10:30 am, and the committee can change the order on the day. The site names no fee and describes no practice session.
first_visit_tips: Plan to arrive around 10:30 am if you are marching, since units gather early.
Staging areas get crowded and parking is limited, so plan a ride or transit.
Report to a division captain, who wears an orange vest, when you arrive.
Do not hold impromptu performances, since they slow the parade.

records.notes: The 'replies by November 13' date from tier 1 sits in a note about vendors, so it is no longer named as a parade deadline. The order of march page shows no year, so its assembly time is presented as usual timing, not a 2026 fact. The 2026 application form is a fillable PDF whose field labels could not be read, so its contents are not described. Banner carriers get 6 community service hours, but no page says a service hours letter is given, so that stays unknown.

records.name: Mekom Torah
records.summary: An online study group for Jewish adults, with beginner Hebrew courses and reading groups. Its Exploring Judaism discussion series is on sabbatical until fall 2027.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a Hebrew course or join a reading group. Exploring Judaism, a discussion series that needs no Hebrew, is paused until fall 2027.

schedule.text: Reading the Tradition in Hebrew meets every other Sunday, and the site lists no time for it. Exploring Judaism is on sabbatical until fall 2027; when it runs, it meets two Thursdays a month from 2 to 3:15 pm Eastern, on Zoom, October through May.

cost.text: Suggested donations, not fixed fees: $200 for the 12-session How to Read Hebrew course and $360 for an Exploring Judaism series. You can give more or less.

first_step.how: Fill in the sign-up form on the How to Read Hebrew course page, or call 610-368-4065 with questions.
first_step.basis: The How to Read Hebrew course is written for people new to Hebrew, and the page explains how to sign up. The home page says Exploring Judaism needs no Hebrew to join.
first_step.what_to_expect: Courses meet on Zoom, and sessions are recorded for anyone who misses one. How to Read Hebrew has twelve sessions on Monday evenings from 7 to 8:15 pm Eastern, with all materials provided. Exploring Judaism is a discussion led by Rabbi Helen Plotkin, and you get the Zoom link after you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Set up Zoom on your phone or computer before the first session.
Fill in the form with your name, email, and a few words about yourself, as the page asks.
Call 610-368-4065 if you are not sure which course fits your level.

records.notes: Exploring Judaism is on sabbatical until fall 2027 according to its page, so the summary and schedule say so. The home page lists How to Read Hebrew as open for enrollment with a September 28, 2026 start, which is before today; the next course start was not found, so check the course page before sending anyone. The about page names no city. The mailing address is in West Townshend, Vermont, and the phone is a 610 number. Programs are open to anyone online, but the site does not say it serves Philadelphia specifically, so the orchestrator should decide whether this online-only group belongs in the directory (verdict kept at publish from tier 1). The email address sits behind a protected link and was not recorded.

records.name: Mekor Habracha (Center City Synagogue)
records.summary: A congregation at 1500 Walnut Street that welcomes visitors. It runs daily minyanim and classes on its davening schedule, a monthly Tot Shabbat for young children, and a WhatsApp group.
records.what_you_do: Join the WhatsApp group or the newsletter, come to the monthly Tot Shabbat for young children, attend a minyan or class on the davening schedule, or sponsor a Kiddush.

schedule.text: Weekday morning and evening prayers, Shabbat morning services from 9:15 am, and a Tot Shabbat on the last Shabbat of each month, about 11 am. Times shift with the seasons, so check the davening schedule.

cost.text: Membership for the 2026 to 2027 year: single $1,000, couple or family $2,000, student $500, plus a suggested $100 security fee. Payment plans are available, and the shul says no one is turned away for lack of funds. The page does not say whether visitors pay to attend services.

first_step.how: Email admin@mekorhabracha.org with 'Join Us' in the subject line to join the WhatsApp group, then come to a service on the davening schedule.
first_step.basis: The homepage says visitors are welcome and gives a WhatsApp route and a newsletter sign-up. The visit page does not describe a first visit or say whether you must register.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit in detail, so the office is the best place to ask what to expect. Shabbat morning prayers begin at 9:15 am, and a hot kiddush follows around 11:30 am. The page says the shul welcomes members and nonmembers alike, but it does not say what visitors pay.
first_visit_tips: Call the office at 215-525-4246 before your first visit to ask what to wear and which entrance to use.
Check the davening schedule for current times, since winter times differ from summer.
If cost is a concern, ask about the payment plans the page says are available.

records.notes: The davening page's newest dated item is a Selichot schedule for September 2026, which sets last_sign_of_life. Weekday evening prayers are listed at 6:30 pm, but winter weekday evening prayers run only with enough interest, so check before going. Class audiences and times are not stated, and the class dates shown are one-time events. The Tot Shabbat age range is not stated, and registration is through a log in page. The visit page does not say whether a visit needs registration. Membership amounts are the 2026 to 2027 figures from the membership page.

records.name: Memorial Presbyterian Church of Fox Chase
records.summary: A Presbyterian church in Fox Chase with an 11 am Sunday service, a children's ministry for children of all ages, and Food for Hope, a food pantry that gives out food bags on Saturdays.
records.what_you_do: Attend Sunday worship at 11 am, enroll children in the children's ministry with the registration form, or volunteer through the church's volunteering form. Food for Hope gives food bags on Saturdays to people in Fox Chase and nearby who need them, with no ID required.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am. Food for Hope gives out food bags on Saturdays, and the site gives no hours, so call the church office at 215-745-2844 to ask.

cost.text: The site lists no fees for worship or the children's ministry. It has donation options.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 11 am, or call the church office at 215-745-2844 or email mpcfoxchase@gmail.com to ask about visiting.
first_step.basis: Worship is public and the contact page is the way to ask questions, but the site has no visitor welcome message or new-here steps.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a Sunday visit, so the office is the best place to ask. Worship starts at 11 am. The children's ministry is listed for children of all ages, with Sunday School, Junior Church, and a program called Jesus and Me, but the site gives no session times.
first_visit_tips: Call or email before your first Sunday to ask about parking and which entrance to use, since the site does not say.
For children, use the registration form linked from the children's ministry page.
Ask about accessibility before you come, since the site lists none.

records.notes: Food for Hope details come from its own page: a pantry running since 2009, Saturday visits, and the office phone for anyone who cannot come on a Saturday. The church site has no visitor page and no parking or accessibility details, and the newsletter sign-up shows an error message. The volunteer and registration forms are PDFs that the fetch tool could not read, so volunteer roles are not described. The children's ministry page gives 'all ages' but no ages or times. The Instagram and Facebook URLs are built from the handles the contact page shows.

records.name: Mid-City Youth Athletic Association
records.summary: A youth football and cheerleading league in Philadelphia that plays full-contact games and is enrolled with USA Football for 2026. Each season has a registration window before it starts.
records.what_you_do: Kids register for a season and play league games. The league page does not list volunteer or coach roles.

schedule.text: The league runs in seasons, each with a registration window before it starts. Practice and game days and times are not published.

cost.text: The league page does not state a fee.

first_step.how: Watch the league page for the next registration window and register there during it. No phone, email, or sign-up steps are listed.
first_step.basis: Registration windows are listed, but the league page gives no sign-up steps or contact details, so the way in is unclear. The windows listed for 2026 have already closed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The league plays full-contact football games for kids and teens, and it is enrolled with USA Football for 2026. The page gives no practice times, age divisions, or fees, so ask before you plan a season.
first_visit_tips: Check the league page for the next registration window, since the 2026 windows have closed.
No phone or email is listed, so the league page is the only route found.
Expect to ask about practice days and fees before you sign up.

records.notes: The About section also calls the group the Mid-City Tigers Youth Football and Cheerleading Organization (an alias for matching). One web search (the only one allowed) found no other page, phone, email, or registration page for this league, so none could be recorded. The league page lists 2026 seasons only, and both registration windows have closed by today's date. This is a thin record: the way in is unclear, so a person may want to check before the next season opens.

records.name: Mill Creek Urban Farm
records.summary: An educational urban farm at 49th and Brown Streets in West Philadelphia, founded in 2005 and run as a program of the nonprofit A Little Taste of Everything. It grows and distributes produce and runs farm-based learning for all ages.
records.what_you_do: Fill out the farm's volunteer form (a Google form linked from the site), come to the Saturday market when it is open, or ask about a group visit or the after-school gardening club. Volunteers are asked to wear hats and protective boots.

schedule.text: A Saturday market runs from 12 to 2 pm at the farm and accepts Farmers Market Nutrition Program vouchers. One part of the site also says a farmers market is coming soon, so call first. Volunteer workdays are not scheduled on the site.

cost.text: The site does not list prices for produce or fees for visits.

access.notes: Parking: bike parking and street parking. Buses 30, 52, and 64 serve the area. The site says to walk from the SEPTA Route 10 trolley or from the El stops at 46th and 52nd Streets, but it does not say which is closest.

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer form linked from the farm's site, or email millcreekfarmphilly@gmail.com to ask about workdays or group visits.
first_step.basis: The farm lists a clear volunteer form and two ways to contact it, and its FAQ says youth and other groups can join volunteer workdays. The site does not describe what a first visit is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers join community workdays on the farm and are asked to wear a hat and protective boots. Workday dates are not published, so the form or an email is the way to ask. The Saturday market runs from 12 to 2 pm, but the site says a farmers market is coming soon, so call first.
first_visit_tips: Wear a hat and protective boots, which the site asks volunteers to wear.
Call 267.279.9679 before a Saturday visit to confirm the market is open.
If you are bringing a class, team, or group, ask about visit dates, since the site has no booking page.

records.notes: The site gives two street addresses and ZIP codes. 4901 Brown St, 19139 is used here, and it matches the farm location line. The contact page also shows 49th Brown Street with ZIP 19311, which looks wrong, and a P.O. box with ZIP 19151. Confirm before publishing. The Saturday market is listed with hours but also described as coming soon, so the market status is unknown. The programs page lists six programs with no ages or costs. The FAQ names a weekly after-school gardening club at Martha Washington Elementary and a high school internship through the Philadelphia Youth Network. The event calendar lists nothing. The volunteer Google form was not opened or submitted. The name, founding year, and parent nonprofit from tier 1 were not re-checked in this pass.
